phrases.text: Question 2 asks whether to limit school property tax growth for two years; each ballot fills in local names.
A 2026 state law puts the question on ballots this year and in 2028.
The question needs a three-fifths majority to pass.
The school tax levy could grow only with inflation and new construction.
Central office spending could not exceed 6 percent of district appropriations.
Bonded building costs count toward neither limit.
A district could exceed either limit by a supermajority vote.
New Hampshire's Questions on the General Election Ballot 2026 does not include a cost estimate for the question.
New Hampshire publishes no official argument for the question.
New Hampshire publishes no official argument against the question.
A yes vote is for adopting the limits.
A no vote is against adopting the limits.
